proposals.before: After the usurper Zhu Youzhen seized power, Quan Yu was made military commissioner of Song.
proposals.after: After the commoner (Zhu Yougui) usurped the throne, Quan Yu was made military commissioner of Songzhou.
proposals.reason: Chinese 庶人篡位 refers to Zhu Yougui (友珪), later degraded to commoner, not Zhu Youzhen (末帝).

proposals.before: (The 《Five Dynasties Essentials》 records that Quan Yu was posthumously honored as Minister of Works with the temple name Dejing.
proposals.after: (The 《Five Dynasties Essentials》 records that Quan Yu was posthumously honored as Director of the Imperial Secretariat (尚書令) with the posthumous title Dejing.
proposals.reason: 尚書令 is not Minister of Works (司空), and 諡 marks a posthumous name, not a temple name.

proposals.before: Hu Zhu notes in the 《History of Liang》 biography of Prince Guang that Quan Yu was coarse and habitually addressed the emperor as "Third."
proposals.after: Your subject Hu notes in the 《History of Liang》 biography of Prince Guang that Quan Yu was coarse and habitually addressed the emperor as "Third."
proposals.reason: Chinese has 臣護 only; the added surname Zhu is not in the source.

proposals.before: Pressing the rebel stronghold at Shilou, he charged from a ridge when Wang's line wavered; his horse fell and he died in the melee.
proposals.after: Pressing the rebel stronghold at Shilou, he charged from a ridge when the royal army slightly wavered; his horse fell and he died in the melee.
proposals.reason: 王師 means the royal/imperial army, not a person named Wang.

decisions.reason: Focus 庶人篡位，授宋州節度使 names the usurper only as 庶人 and the post as 宋州節度使. In Later Liang usage 庶人 is Zhu Yougui (友珪) after degradation, not Zhu Youzhen; the prior idiomatic invents the wrong personal name and truncates 宋州 to Song. The proposed wording restores both points without new error.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 庶人篡位，授宋州節度使

decisions.after: (The 《Five Dynasties Essentials》 records that Quan Yu was posthumously honored as Director of the Imperial Secretariat with the posthumous title Dejing.
decisions.reason: Focus 贈尚書令，諡德靖 grants Director of the Imperial Secretariat, not Minister of Works, and 諡 is a posthumous title, not a temple name. The revised replacement corrects both mistranslations without leaving untranslated Chinese in the English field.
Focus 臣護按 names the annotator only as 護 under the self-reference 臣; the prior idiomatic invents the surname Zhu. "Your subject Hu" restores 臣護 without changing the quoted biography content.
Focus 王師小卻 means the royal/imperial army slightly retreated; 王師 is not a person named Wang. The proposed wording corrects that misreading and preserves 小卻 as "slightly wavered."
